nodes.label: User
nodes.summary: Posts, and reads the home feed with cursor pagination.

nodes.label: Post API
nodes.summary: Assigns a time-sortable ID (Instagram: 41-bit time + 13-bit shard + 10-bit sequence), writes the post, and enqueues fan-out.
nodes.details: Instagram generates IDs inside Postgres with a PL/pgSQL function per logical shard (a Postgres schema). Thousands of logical shards map to far fewer physical servers.

nodes.label: Post store (sharded)
nodes.summary: Posts and metadata, partitioned by logical shards. Twitter's real-time store for Tweets is Manhattan.

nodes.label: Follow graph
nodes.summary: Who follows whom. Twitter's social graph, Flock, ran on Gizzard/MySQL with peaks of tens of millions of QPS.

nodes.label: Fan-out queue
nodes.summary: Decouples posting from delivery so the post call returns quickly. The sources we read do not describe Twitter's queueing, so this box is the standard design.

nodes.label: Fanout Service
nodes.summary: Looks up followers and writes the new post's ID into their timeline caches. Idempotent so retries do not duplicate. Very-high-follower accounts are typically skipped and merged at read time.
nodes.details: Twitter's 2017 post names a Fanout Service that writes to the Haplo timeline cache. The hybrid skip rule is a general design and its threshold is not in the sources we read.

nodes.label: Timeline cache (Haplo / Redis)
nodes.summary: Per-user timelines of post IDs in a customised Redis (HybridList). Read by the Timeline Service, written by the Timeline Service and the Fanout Service.
nodes.details: At the time: aggregate 40M–100M commands per second and ~800K service requests per second. Caches protect backing stores from heavy read traffic.

nodes.label: Timeline / Home Mixer
nodes.summary: Builds the feed: candidate generation, feature hydration (~6,000 features), ML scoring, filters and heuristics, mixing with ads and modules, then serving.
nodes.details: Candidate sources named: Earlybird search index (~50% of posts, in-network), Tweet-mixer / Cr Mixer (out-of-network), UTEG interaction graph, Follow Recommendation Service.

nodes.label: Post + user cache
nodes.summary: Hydrates post IDs into full posts and authors at read time, so edits and deletes need no fan-out.

nodes.label: Rankers
nodes.summary: Light Ranker (inside the search index) and Heavy Ranker (neural network) score candidate posts.

steps.caption: The API assigns a time-sortable ID and stores the post in its shard.
It enqueues a fan-out job and returns. Delivery is asynchronous.
A fan-out worker picks up the job.
It looks up the author's followers in the follow graph.
It inserts the post ID into each follower's timeline in the cache. For accounts with very many followers, the hybrid design skips this step and merges at read time.
The client asks for the first page of the feed.
The timeline service reads the user's precomputed list of post IDs.
Posts from very-high-follower accounts the user follows are pulled and merged in (the read side of the hybrid).
Candidates, including out-of-network ones, are scored by the light and heavy rankers.
Post IDs are hydrated into full posts and authors from cache, applying deletes and blocks at read time.
